$comment: The project mail address contract between the Email Worker (deploy/pulumi/src/platform/inbound-mail-worker.js, which routes on it) and the BFF (apps/workspace/bff/inbound-mail/address.ts, which parses and mints it; the office's half of the switch is the inbound-mail WorkOS entitlement). A project address is <localPart>+<slug>.<token>@<domain>, or <localPart>+<token>@<domain> for an empty slug (ADR-0138): one literal Cloudflare routing rule, <localPart>@<domain>, reaches the Worker, and Cloudflare's subaddressing hands it every <localPart>+<detail>@<domain>. localPart and domain are deployment config (INBOUND_MAIL_LOCAL_PART, INBOUND_MAIL_DOMAIN); the values here are the ones every case is run with. A recipient is a project address when, after stripping surrounding angle brackets and the quotes of a quoted local part, and ASCII lowercasing: the domain equals domain, the local part has a +, the text before the FIRST + equals localPart, and the text after the LAST dot of the subaddress (or the whole subaddress) matches tokenPattern. Both sides run every case below in their specs (inbound-mail-worker.spec.ts, address.spec.ts), so neither can change the rule alone.

cases.note: a project whose name has nothing Latin in it: the bare token
senders' clients change case, the prefix's and the domain's too
only the text after the last dot counts; the slug is decoration
the base address of the routing rule carries no token
no subaddress: the address form before the subdomain move is not accepted
another prefix: p, the default local part before project, is not accepted
the parent domain is not the receiving domain
nor is a subdomain of it
nor a look-alike that starts with it
1 is not in the base32 alphabet
only the text after the last dot counts
the subaddress is everything after the first +, so a second + lands in the token position
the Kelvin sign must not fold onto k
